turns.said: The kids love the camera part.
turns.answer: Children often enjoy seeing a robot look at things.

turns.said: I'm allergic to cats.
turns.answer: Thanks for sharing, I will remember that you are allergic to cats.

turns.said: I coach the school chess club on Tuesdays.
turns.answer: Chess club on Tuesdays sounds like a good tradition.

turns.said: What's the biggest number of things you can remember?
turns.answer: I can hold many thousands of memories, and the limit depends on the device storage.

turns.said: Do you get things wrong?
turns.answer: Yes, sometimes, so I show the memory I used to answer.

turns.said: Where do robots like you get used?
turns.answer: Edge style systems suit robots, phones, cars, and sensors that cannot always reach a server.

turns.said: My husband's name is Marcus.
turns.answer: Marcus is a good name, I will remember it.

turns.said: Thank you, the students learned a lot.
turns.answer: I am glad the students enjoyed it.

turns.said: Hi robot, I'm Jonas.
turns.answer: Hello Jonas, welcome.

turns.said: I interned at Vexalto last summer, a cold chain sensor startup.
turns.answer: An internship at a sensor startup is great experience.

turns.said: I live in Rotterdam.
turns.answer: Rotterdam has great architecture.

turns.said: My sister's dog is called Biscuit.
turns.answer: Biscuit is a great name for a dog.

turns.said: I work as a backend engineer at a bank in Frankfurt.
turns.answer: Backend work at a bank needs careful engineering.

turns.said: My team has nine engineers.
turns.answer: Nine engineers is a solid team.

turns.said: I'm running the Berlin marathon too, aiming for under 4 hours.
turns.answer: Good luck, the Berlin course is fast.

turns.said: Do you stay offline?
turns.answer: Yes, I work offline, and all models run on my Jetson.

turns.said: What did HNSW stand for?
turns.answer: HNSW stands for Hierarchical Navigable Small World, a graph based index.

turns.said: I'm building a smart garden with 6 moisture sensors.
turns.answer: Six sensors is a good start for a garden.

turns.said: My sensors talk over LoRaWAN every five minutes.
turns.answer: LoRaWAN is a good fit for low power sensors.

turns.said: I drink my coffee with milk and sugar.
turns.answer: That is a classic way to drink coffee.

turns.said: What is a sparse vector?
turns.answer: A sparse vector stores only its non zero values.

turns.said: What are payload filters?
turns.answer: A payload filter limits a search to points whose stored fields match.

turns.said: My train is at 8:15.
turns.answer: An 8:15 train is a good time to start the day.

turns.said: Thanks and goodbye.
turns.answer: Goodbye Jonas.

turns.said: Hello, I'm Rina.
turns.answer: Hello Rina, welcome.

turns.said: I design robot grippers at a company in Hamburg.
turns.answer: Gripper design is a nice mix of mechanics and software.

turns.said: We run ROS 2 Jazzy on everything.
turns.answer: ROS 2 Jazzy is a newer release with long term support.

turns.said: Our gripper lifts 12 kg.
turns.answer: Twelve kilograms is a strong gripper.

turns.said: I'm giving a talk at PyData Amsterdam on April 2.
turns.answer: Good luck with the talk on April second.

turns.said: My thesis is about speech recognition for Dutch.
turns.answer: Dutch speech recognition is a useful topic.

turns.said: I'm a student at Utrecht University.
turns.answer: Utrecht University is a well known school.

turns.said: My game is called Paper Lanterns and I'm using Unity.
turns.answer: Paper Lanterns sounds like a cozy game.

turns.said: We plan a Steam release on October 3.
turns.answer: October third is a clear release date.

turns.said: I have two cats, Miso and Tofu.
turns.answer: Miso and Tofu are great names for cats.

turns.said: Our 3D printer is called Widget.
turns.answer: Widget is a fun name for a printer.

turns.said: What happens if I ask you to forget me?
turns.answer: I delete every memory linked to you.

turns.said: How long do you remember things?
turns.answer: Ordinary conversation memories last twelve hours.

turns.said: What is a collection in Qdrant?
turns.answer: A collection is a named set of points with the same vector setup.

turns.said: How do you keep visitors' memories apart?
turns.answer: Each stored statement has a visitor id, and every search filters by it.

turns.said: Bye now.
turns.answer: Goodbye Rina.

turns.said: Hey, I'm Pavel.
turns.answer: Hey Pavel, welcome.

turns.said: I'm a security analyst at a bank in Prague.
turns.answer: Security analysis at a bank is an important job.

turns.said: My homelab has 4 Raspberry Pi nodes running Docker Swarm.
turns.answer: Four Pi nodes make a neat little cluster.

turns.said: I climb at a gym called Climbstation.
turns.answer: Climbing is a great way to stay fit.

turns.said: I'm a product manager at a payments startup in Berlin.
turns.answer: Payments is a busy field.

turns.said: We have 120 employees.
turns.answer: A hundred and twenty people is a mid sized company.

turns.said: My flight to Madrid leaves at 9:30 on Friday.
turns.answer: Have a good flight on Friday.

turns.said: I teach computer science at a high school in Brno.
turns.answer: Teaching computer science is rewarding.

turns.said: I have 31 students in my class.
turns.answer: Thirty one students is a big class.

turns.said: My wife's name is Lenka.
turns.answer: Lenka is a lovely name.

turns.said: I'm allergic to dogs.
turns.answer: Thanks, I will remember that you are allergic to dogs.

turns.said: How much does Edge cost?
turns.answer: I do not have current pricing, so please check the Qdrant website.

turns.said: How do snapshots work?
turns.answer: A snapshot is a copy of a shard that you can restore on another device.

turns.said: Who built you?
turns.answer: The Qdrant team built me to demo Edge.

turns.said: How do you remember things?
turns.answer: I turn words into numbers and Edge finds the closest stored notes.

turns.said: I work night shifts sometimes.
turns.answer: Night shifts can be tiring.

turns.said: Bye.
turns.answer: Goodbye Pavel.
